title: Muscles of the lower face, lips and chin

queue.claim: Legan & Burstone (1980) soft-tissue norms used as fitting priors: mentolabial sulcus depth 4 ± 2 mm (B' to Li–Pog'), lower-lip protrusion 2 ± 1 mm and upper-lip protrusion 3 ± 1 mm (to Sn–Pog'), interlabial gap 2 ± 2 mm, vertical lip–chin ratio 1:2
queue.query: Legan Burstone 1980 soft tissue cephalometric analysis orthognathic surgery norms mentolabial sulcus lower lip protrusion interlabial gap

queue.claim: Adult soft-tissue depth over bone (ranges of published means): labrale inferius 11–16 mm, supramentale 9–13 mm, pogonion 9–13 mm, gnathion 7–10 mm, menton 5–9 mm; Holdaway soft-tissue chin thickness 10–12 mm
queue.query: facial soft tissue depth adults pooled means labrale inferius mentolabial sulcus pogonion menton Stephan Simpson 2008

queue.claim: The modiolus centre sits about 10–15 mm lateral to the mouth corner (cheilion), within about ±5 mm vertically; the cadaver DAO insertion is about 10 mm lateral and 10 mm caudal to the commissure (PubMed 33565832)
queue.query: modiolus location distance lateral to oral commissure mm cadaver ultrasound depressor anguli oris insertion

queue.claim: Mentolabial angle norm is about 110–135° (centre about 120–130°, more acute in men), and the lower lip sits 2 ± 2 mm behind Ricketts' E-line in white adults, with more protrusive lips in African and East Asian samples
